title: Food banks in the UK
paragraphs: When looking at Western Europe, we don't usually think about poverty – but in fact, some people in modern-day Britain are so hard up that they can't afford to buy food.

Back in 2008, the financial crisis caused a lot of redundancies. Then there were the cuts to the welfare system in 2013 which added to the problem – and many British people fell into debt. It's estimated that 500,000 people in the UK have turned to food banks, just to get by.

Steph Hagen, who works in a Nottingham food bank, says: "People do not go to a food bank because it's an open door. It's a case of they go to it because they need to. With our food bank – we are an independent one, and we have limited stocks – everyone who comes through our door has no income whatsoever."

There are checks and referrals to make sure nobody is abusing the system. If a doctor or a social worker thinks someone needs to use a food bank – even for a short time – they can give them vouchers. Then the people in need take the vouchers along to the food bank and they get handouts for three days.
Churches and individual donors provide most of the food in the banks. But some businesses might help out too.

And what sort of food is offered in food banks? Hagen says: "Basically, we've got porridge. We do occasionally get fresh produce but it's very rare, especially in the winter months. It's like, tinned fruit, tinned ready meals. We have to give out 'no-cooking' food parcels because people can't afford the gas and electricity".

Community spirit has a lot to do with food banks. Volunteers say they are a great meeting place for people who are lonely and depressed. And when facing a crisis, some beneficiaries might need to feed not only their belly – but also their soul.

vocabulary.entry: poverty /ˈpɒvəti/ n. 贫穷；贫困
vocabulary.example: They live in extreme poverty.
vocabulary.translation: 他们生活在极度贫困之中。

vocabulary.entry: hard up /hɑːd ʌp/ 拮据的；穷困的（短语）（口语词汇）

vocabulary.translation: 那时候我们手头紧。

vocabulary.entry: financial crisis /faɪˈnænʃl ˈkraɪsɪs/ 金融危机（短语）
vocabulary.example: The country was hit by a severe financial crisis.
vocabulary.translation: 该国遭遇了严重的金融危机。

vocabulary.entry: redundancy /rɪˈdʌndənsi/ n. 裁员；失业
vocabulary.example: Many workers faced redundancy due to the crisis.
vocabulary.translation: 危机导致许多工人面临裁员。

vocabulary.entry: welfare system /ˈwelfeə ˈsɪstəm/ 福利体系（短语）
vocabulary.example: The government cut funding to the welfare system.
vocabulary.translation: 政府削减了福利体系的资金。

vocabulary.entry: fall into debt /fɔːl ˈɪntu det/ 负债；陷入债务（短语）

vocabulary.entry: estimate /ˈestɪmeɪt/ v. 估算；预计

vocabulary.example: She struggles to get by on a low income.
vocabulary.translation: 她靠低收入勉强维持生计。

vocabulary.entry: independent /ˌɪndɪˈpendənt/ adj. 独立的

vocabulary.translation: 这是一家无政府资助的独立食物银行。

vocabulary.entry: limited stocks /ˈlɪmɪted stɒks/ 有限储备（短语）
vocabulary.example: The charity has limited stocks of food in winter.
vocabulary.translation: 该慈善机构冬季食物储备有限。

vocabulary.entry: income /ˈɪŋkʌm/ n. 收入
vocabulary.example: He has no income and relies entirely on help.
vocabulary.translation: 他没有收入，完全依靠救助。

vocabulary.entry: referral /rɪˈfɜːrəl/ n. 转交；资质审核
vocabulary.example: You need a referral from a social worker to use the service.
vocabulary.translation: 使用该服务需要社工的资质审核证明。

vocabulary.entry: abuse the system /əˈbjuːz ðə ˈsɪstəm/ 滥用制度（短语）
vocabulary.example: Strict checks prevent people from abusing the system.
vocabulary.translation: 严格核查防止有人滥用制度。

vocabulary.entry: voucher /ˈvaʊtʃə(r)/ n. 凭证；救助券
vocabulary.example: The doctor gave her a voucher for the food bank.
vocabulary.translation: 医生给了她一张食物银行救助券。

vocabulary.entry: handout /ˈhændaʊt/ n. 救济品；援助物资

vocabulary.translation: 当地企业捐赠食物提供接济。

vocabulary.entry: porridge /ˈpɒrɪdʒ/ n. 粥；麦片粥

vocabulary.entry: community spirit /kəˈmjuːnəti ˈspɪrɪt/ 社区互助精神（短语）
vocabulary.example: Community spirit is strong in this neighborhood.
vocabulary.translation: 这个社区的互助精神很强。

vocabulary.entry: depressed /dɪˈprest/ adj. 消沉的；抑郁的

vocabulary.translation: 他失业后感到很消沉。

vocabulary.translation: 食物银行的受助者大多是低收入家庭。
